headline: NATO begins 2029 capability-target talks with 'without the US' openly debated
dek: NATO has begun talks this month on the forces/weapons allies need against a Russian attack, setting capability targets for 2029 (first phase of the NDPP cycle; Political Guidance due in coming days). Explicitly on the table: how much Europe can do without the US, as the Trump administration weighs…
sources: Politico (15 current/former NATO officials and diplomats; Adm. Pierre Vandier quoted); German Chancellor Friedrich Merz (interview, biz.chosun relay)
fault_line: NATO is now formally planning for a Europe without America — while its nuclear exercise flies over Italy. Is this prudence, or an admission the alliance is already drifting?

sections.what_happened: NATO has begun talks this month on the forces/weapons allies need against a Russian attack, setting capability targets for 2029 (first phase of the NDPP cycle; Political Guidance due in coming days). Explicitly on the table: how much Europe can do without the US, as the Trump administration weighs a sharp reduction of US forces in Europe. Merz: warns Russia targets European democracy, says Europe must become 'strong enough to defend ourselves within NATO,' reducing security dependence on the US; he tries to persuade Trump that Europe's stability is in US interest. (NATO's Steadfast Noon nuclear exercise continued over Italy today — routine annual, monitor only.)
sections.what_verified: Politico mirrors (scoopfeeds/mingooland), NATO NDPP-cycle context; Merz interview relay.
sections.what_disputed: No US official has confirmed a Europe drawdown; the 'without the US' discussion is planning-scenario work, not a decision.
sections.why_matters: The alliance of record is doing scenario planning against its own biggest member: NATO's 2029 capability targets will be drawn up with 'what Europe can do without the US' explicitly on the table. Merz says it out loud — strong enough to defend ourselves within NATO. Washington hasn't confirmed any drawdown; the planning is happening anyway.
sections.context: Background: NATO begins 2029 capability-target talks with 'without the US' openly debated; Merz: Europe must defend itself within NATO

totw_analysis: Our read: The alliance of record is doing scenario planning against its own biggest member: NATO's 2029 capability targets will be drawn up with 'what Europe can do without the US' explicitly on the table. Merz says it out loud — strong enough to defend ourselves within NATO. Washington hasn't confirmed any drawdown; the planning is happening anyway. The fault line our audience is arguing over: NATO is now formally planning for a Europe without America — while its nuclear exercise flies over Italy. Is this prudence, or an admission the alliance is already drifting?
